full_judgment: 2. The petitioners as pre-emptee filed Miscellaneous Case No. 68 of 1989 for pre-emption under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Chandpur, which was subsequently re-numbered as Misc. Case No. 14 of 1990 on transfer to the Court of the Additional Assistant Judge, Chandpur. The petitioners' case, in short, is that they are co-sharers to the case jote while the pre-emptee is a stranger purchaser thereto. It was further contended that the pre-emptee secretly purchased the case land from opposite party No. 2 by the impugned kabala dated 26-1-88 without serving any notice upon them and it was only on 29-6-89, when the pre-emptee opposite party No. 1 came to clear bushes in the case land, the pre-emptors came to learn about the disputed transfer for the first time and after obtaining the certified copy of the disputed kabala they promptly filed the present case for pre-emption.
